verdict.rationale: Bento lets users write alert rules in plain English. These rules compile to trace queries, fire in real time on detected signals, and automatically route to Slack, PagerDuty, email, or webhook. It also documents reusable trigger-based fixes (skills, subagents, tools), with skills and rules stored in the repo as Markdown and YAML. Missing for 10: documentation of the rule/trigger configuration schema and of action types beyond notification routing, detail on how trigger-based fixes are wired to events, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can define rules that trigger actions automatically on events

citations.quote: Alerts are defined in plain natural language... Rules compile to trace queries and route to Slack, PagerDuty, email, or webhook.
Describe a failure mode in plain English. Bento trains a detector on your own traces, fires it in real time, and backfills your history.
Reusable, trigger-based fixes: skills, subagents, and tools that graduate from candidate to promote as they prove themselves in production.
